issues.failure_explanation: Since a = kappa^{-1} mu, sum_q a_{pq} psi_q = sum_r [kappa^{-1}]_{pr} w_r psi_r, which equals w_p for all p iff kappa w = w∘psi (componentwise). This is not implied by kappa·1 = psi (the second relation), so the proof's stated equivalence between the first and second relations is invalid; the weights w_q do not factor out row-wise (they do column-wise, which is why the fourth relation sum_p a_{pq} psi~_p = w_q is true). Concretely for N = 2, with psi = (5/6+√15/6, −2/3, 5/6−√15/6) and the paper's own Butcher row a_{0·} = (29/180, 8/45−√15/15, 29/180−√15/30), one gets sum_q a_{0q} psi_q ≈ 0.2979 ≠ w_0 = 5/18 ≈ 0.2778; equivalently [kappa w]_0 = psi_0/6 + 5√15/81 ≈ 0.4856 ≠ w_0 psi_0 ≈ 0.4108. The relation holds only trivially for N = 1 where w is constant.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the relation sum_q a_{pq} psi_q = w_p from the lemma and the corresponding lines and false equivalence from the proof; keep the second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth relations with their (valid) proofs.
issues.overall_effect: The first identity in (eq:ader_int_prop) is false for N ≥ 2. The remaining relations (kappa·1 = psi, 1^T kappa = psi~^T, the column identity used in (eq:ader_dg_node_sol_by_q), and the trace identity) are correct and are the only ones used elsewhere, so no downstream result is invalidated.
issues.title: First relation of Lemma ader_int_prop (a·psi = w) is false for N ≥ 2; proof's claimed equivalence is invalid
issues.why_classification: A stated identity must be withdrawn as false, so not every claim survives; but the loss is contained to one relation of a technical lemma with no dependents, leaving a recognizably comparable result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: However, conditions $C(N+1)$, $D(N+1)$, which are inherent in the classical GL method are not satisfied, but the deviations decrease with $N$
Lemma~\ref{lemma:p_ode_exact} shows that $\mathbf{q}$ is exact solution only in case $L < N$, and in case $L \geq N$ the local solution $\mathbf{q}$ is not an exact solution.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary's conclusion (not a collocation method) is derived from the assertion that C(N+1) fails. Nowhere in the paper is this proven for general N: it is supported only by mpmath numerics for N ≤ 75, and the remark in the proof of Lemma cn_cond that stage values are inexact for L ≥ N does not follow from Lemma p_ode_exact (non-representability of the exact solution in span{phi_p} does not imply the nodal values are inexact). Order p_RK > s alone does not exclude collocation (GL collocation has order 2s).

failure_location.quote: since it has the convergence order $p_{\rm RK} > s$ and the simplifying condition $C(N+1)$ is not satisfied.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Justify failure of C(N+1) rigorously, e.g.: if C(N+1) held with the GL nodes, Theorem 7.7 of Hairer would make the method the GL collocation method, whose stability function is R_{N+1,N+1}, contradicting Theorem pade_approx / L-stability (or the order 2N+1 exactness).
issues.overall_effect: As written the corollary is unsupported for general N; the statement itself is true and can be justified from later results.
issues.title: Corollary rk_is_not_coll rests on the unproven premise that C(N+1) fails
issues.why_classification: A short argument available from results already in the paper closes the gap; no claim is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed bound is the classical error of the Lagrange interpolant of ũ at the nodes t_{n,p}. But q_n = sum_p q̂_{n,p} phi_p has nodal values q̂_{n,p} which are stage values of the implicit RK method, not ũ(t_{n,p}); the bound applies to q_n only if |q̂_{n,p} − ũ(t_{n,p})| = O(Δt^{N+1}) is established (stage order N, which follows from C(N) but is never invoked) together with a Lebesgue-constant argument. Lemma p_ode_exact, cited as justification, concerns only u' = f(t) with polynomial f of degree < N and says nothing about general F(u,t). Additionally, |u_n − u(t_n)| is the accumulated global error O(Δt^{2N+1}), not the one-step local error O(Δt^{2N+2}) as claimed (immaterial to the final rate).

failure_location.quote: which is also applicable for sufficiently smooth functions $\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{u}, t)$ due to the Lemma~\ref{lemma:p_ode_exact}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert a stage-error argument: by Lemma cn_cond the method has stage order N, so q̂_{n,p} − ũ(t_{n,p}) = O(Δt_n^{N+1}) (standard RK stage-order result); then |q_n − ũ| ≤ Λ_N max_p|q̂_{n,p} − ũ(t_{n,p})| + interpolation error, both O(Δt_n^{N+1}); correct the exponent 2N+2 to 2N+1.
issues.overall_effect: The N+1 order of the local solution (Lemma, Theorems on L_inf and L_q norms, Corollary on nodal points) is unproven as written; the results are consistent with the numerics and are expected to hold via stage-order theory.
issues.title: Lemma local_sol_order_L_inf applies the Lagrange interpolation error bound to q_n, which does not interpolate the reference solution
issues.why_classification: A replacement argument (stage order plus interpolation stability) is needed rather than a local fix, but it is contained and standard, and all statements and rates survive.

issues.failure_explanation: From the preceding correct display ∫|u_L−u|^q ≤ ||u_L−u||_∞^q·|Ω| one obtains ||u_L−u||_{L_q} ≤ |Ω|^{1/q}||u_L−u||_∞, not [|Ω|^{-1}||·||_∞^q]^{1/q}. The stated intermediate inequality is false whenever |Ω| > 1 (e.g. |Ω| = 4π or 10 in the paper's examples), and the derived constant C_q = C/|Ω|^{1/q} is wrong; the correct constant is C|Ω|^{1/q}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 1/|Ω| by |Ω| and C/|Ω|^{1/q} by C|Ω|^{1/q}.
issues.overall_effect: The existential statement of the theorem remains true (a constant exists), but the explicit constant and the displayed inequality are incorrect.
issues.title: Wrong |Omega| factor in the L_q estimate of Theorem local_sol_order_L_p
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction restores a valid derivation with the same rate and conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The matrix $a = \kappa^{-1}\cdot\mu$ in the denominator is invertible and $\mathrm{rank}(a) = N+1$. The denominator of $R(z)$ is a polynomial $R_{N, N+1}(z)$ of degree $N$.
Symbolic calculations in the \texttt{Maple} for degrees $N = 1,\, \ldots,\, 6$ showed that the function $R(z)$ coincides with the $(N, N+1)$-Pad\'{e} approximation of $\exp(z)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Knowing only that R(z) is a rational function with numerator degree ≤ N and denominator degree N+1 does not identify it as the (N,N+1)-Padé approximant of exp(z); one also needs exp(z) − R(z) = O(z^{2N+2}) and the uniqueness of Padé approximants. The proof never establishes this approximation order (it would follow from Theorem order_rk, which is not invoked). Moreover the degree statements are internally inconsistent: invertible a gives det(I − za) of degree N+1 (not N), and rank(a − 1w^T) = N gives numerator degree at most N (not N−1); rank alone does not fix the degree of det(I − zB) exactly. The stated numbers would correspond to an (N−1,N) approximant, contradicting the theorem's own conclusion.

failure_location.quote: Therefore the numerator of $R(z)$ is a polynomial $P_{N, N+1}(z)$ of degree $N-1$. It follows that $R(z)$ is the $(N, N+1)$-Pad\'{e} approximation $R_{N, N+1}(z)$ of $\exp(z)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the degrees (denominator exactly N+1 since a is invertible; numerator ≤ N since a − 1w^T is singular), add that by Theorem order_rk exp(z) − R(z) = O(z^{2N+2}), and conclude by uniqueness of the (N,N+1) Padé approximant.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem pade_approx is unproven as written; Theorem l2_stab_rk, cor:added-2 and the L-stability part of coroll:ader_dg_stabs rest on it. The statement is true and repairable from Theorem order_rk, after which cor:added-3 can no longer serve as an independent proof of the order (see ISSUE-006).
issues.title: Proof of Theorem pade_approx infers the Padé property from polynomial degrees alone, with misstated degrees
issues.why_classification: The missing step is a short, standard argument using a result already proven in the paper; all conclusions and dependent stability results survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the residual term of the $R_{N, N+1}(z)$ is $\exp(z) - R_{N, N+1}(z) = O(z^{2N+2})$

issues.failure_explanation: exp(z) − R(z) = O(z^{p+1}) is only a necessary condition for an RK method to have order p (it is the order on the scalar linear test equation); many RK methods have a stability function approximating exp to higher order than their classical order. Hence the residual of R_{N,N+1} does not prove p_RK = 2N+1 for the general nonlinear IVP (eq:ivp_ode_diff_src), and the corollary does not constitute an alternative proof of Theorem order_rk. Furthermore, the only source-supported way to complete the proof of Theorem pade_approx (ISSUE-005) uses Theorem order_rk, so the purported alternative proof would in any case be circular.

failure_location.quote: so the approximation order of the IRK-GL-ADER-DG method $p_{\rm RK} = 2N+1$, which is an alternative proof of Theorem~\ref{theorem:order_rk}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the corollary to state that the Padé residual shows R(z) approximates exp(z) to order 2N+1 (order on linear problems), consistent with and necessary for, but not a proof of, Theorem order_rk; remove the phrase 'alternative proof'.
issues.overall_effect: The claim of an independent second proof of the order 2N+1 is unsupported; Theorem order_rk itself stands on its own proof via Butcher's simplifying conditions.
issues.title: cor:added-3 invalidly infers RK order from the stability function order and is circular with the Padé theorem
issues.why_classification: The corollary's advertised content (an independent proof of the order theorem) must be withdrawn and replaced by a weaker consistency statement; no other result depends on it.
